belief_statement: Cognitive performance has inconsistent effects on cognitive performance. This conclusion draws on 19 findings from 16 independent studies.

latent_variables.name: Individual sensitivity differences
latent_variables.rationale: High heterogeneity (high) across findings suggests an unmeasured individual-difference variable moderates the effect of cognitive performance on cognitive performance.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Pre-screening for trait sensitivity or prior exposure

latent_variables.name: Mechanism selection
latent_variables.rationale: Multiple mechanisms are implicated (Psychophysics / Perception, Distraction Theory). A latent variable may determine which pathway is activated.

latent_variables.name: Dose and duration
latent_variables.rationale: Most studies measure presence/absence of cognitive performance, not dose-response curves. Duration and intensity likely matter.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Parametric variation of intensity and exposure duration

research_needs.question: What moderates the effect of cognitive performance on cognitive performance?
research_needs.rationale: High heterogeneity suggests an unmeasured moderator.

research_needs.question: Which mechanism best explains cognitive performance → cognitive performance?
research_needs.rationale: 2 candidate mechanisms exist. Process tracing would identify the active pathway.

research_needs.question: What is the dose-response curve for cognitive performance effects on cognitive performance?
research_needs.rationale: Dose-response data enables design guidelines with specific thresholds.

research_needs.question: Do the effects of cognitive performance on cognitive performance persist over weeks/months?
research_needs.rationale: Most findings are from acute studies. Long-term effects are unknown.
